items.title: This Cyberpunk 2077 mod makes Night City’s rain fall in 3D, and lightning finally strikes
items.summary: Torrent, a new Cyberpunk 2077 mod by CyanideX, swaps the game's flat rain for 3D drops, and adds branching lightning, wind-driven storms, and tyre spray.
items.content:
Image credit: CDPR / Torrent News by Vikki Blake Contributor Published on Nov. 15, 2026, 5:39 p.m. Follow Cyberpunk 2077 Prioritise us on Google A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming , modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods .

We recently learned that Cyberpunk 2 might be trying to revive Cyberpunk 2077’s online ambitions, as a new CD Projekt Red job listing is looking for someone familiar with "multiplayer network architecture" .

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Replacement Officially Arrives 2027 With Huge Sci-Fi Open World
items.summary: Brace yourself! A new cyberpunk adventure with no rules is coming—find out why fans are buzzing!
items.content:
NO LAW Neon Giant Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Angharad Redden Published Nov 15, 2026, 6:00 AM EST Known as 'Cyberpunk 2077's' biggest fan, Angharad is a Welsh games writer who thrives in anything related to digital storytelling. If a video game explores the intricacies and horrors of womanhood, she is there. Thanks to previous work at GAMINGbible, GameByte, The Loadout, Game Luster, Angharad has built a strong understanding of both the digital world and what fans want from it and is eager to share her thoughts and expertise with readers. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Despite some of its difficulties at launch, there is no denying that Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the most loved games of the past decade. Taking players to a dystopian, neon-soaked future filled with chaos, technology, and Keanu Reeves, the CD Projekt RED RPG is still praised to this day, especially as it has since welcomed multiple free updates and the award-winning Phantom Liberty DLC.

Now, almost six years on from launch, and fans are eagerly awaiting the launch of the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, but with CDPR being hard at work on The Witcher IV first, we are still many years away from the highly anticipated release.

However, it is not all doom and gloom as, to absolutely nobody's surprise, Cyberpunk 2077 has gone onto inspire many future releases, and one such example is NO LAW.

Set to launch in 2027, NO LAW is an upcoming open-world cyberpunk RPG by Neon Giant. Players will take on the role of Grey Harker, an ex-military personnel attempting to live a quiet life after facing life-threatening injuries on the field. However, in Port Desire, there is no such thing as a quiet life, especially when there are no laws to govern its citizens. As such, Grey finds himself back in the fray when trouble finds its way to his door.

NO LAW is a first-person, story rich, cyber-noire shooter set in a decadent port city built on neon sleaze instead of regulations. Explore its rich history and meet the veiled hearts of the city as you take back what was wrongfully taken from you.

Despite taking place in a city with no laws, your actions will still have consequences, and as you meet colorful characters along the way, it will be up to you if you make them friend or foe. However, with multiple paths to take and many endings to achieve, no two playthroughs will be the same, and replayability is encouraged.

With Night City being one of the most iconic gaming settings of all time, it seems as though Port Desire will not be far behind. The "industrial cybergrunge city, lush with greenery and overflowing with personalities" is a hub for import and export, and it is where all walks of life flock to try and make it big. As such, it will become your playground, whether you go all guns blazing or without making a sound. You will be able to take the law into your own hands, but be careful where you step, and who you step on.

NO LAW Neon Giant Master the tools, learn the systems, and turn every mission into your own story. Will you utilize Grey’s tactical background and stick to the shadows, or will you let him give in to his unbridled rage and go in guns blazing? Whether you prefer the tactical route or revel in the destruction left in your wake, make sure you take the time to explore the variety of military upgrades available to you. Outsmart enemies with sci-fi devices, vertical movement, or full-frontal chaos.

As mentioned, NO LAW does not yet have an exact release date, but we can expect the cyberpunk RPG to hit Steam some time in the new year. So, if you are feeling the pain of having to wait for the launch of the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, look no further than this upcoming gem.

GTA VI Owner Takes a Shot at Cyberpunk 2077, Recalls the RPG’s Disastrous Launch, and Believes Delaying Rockstar’s Game Was the Best Decision
items.summary: Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, defended delaying the release of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' to November 2026 to ensure its quality, drawing a comparison to the problematic launch of 'Cyberpunk 2077'. He emphasized the importance of making tough decisions to maintain high standards in game development, contrasting Rockstar's approach with those who rush releases despite potential issues.
items.content:
In an alternate reality, Grand Theft Auto VI would have launched late last year. We know that never happened, as the game suffered two delays that pushed its release to November 2026. Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, acknowledges that changing the schedule was a difficult decision, but ultimately believes it was the best thing they could have done.

To make his point, the executive behind Rockstar Games’ parent company brought up a particularly infamous case: Cyberpunk 2077 , which had one of the most disastrous and controversial launches of the decade.

GTA VI was first revealed to the world in December 2023, when its release was confirmed for sometime in fall 2025. Unfortunately, the developers later announced the first delay, pushing its debut to May of the following year.

Just when everything seemed to be going smoothly, Rockstar Games once again took to social media to announce a second change to the release date. Grand Theft Auto VI will now arrive in stores on November 19, and everything seems to indicate that nothing and no one will prevent it from launching on the scheduled date.

In mid-October, studio head Jennifer Kolbe spoke with Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier and recalled the moment she had to inform Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two Interactive, about the second delay. “I think he said something like, ‘I can’t believe it! Please tell me you’re joking!’”

In the end, Jennifer Kolbe described the head of Rockstar Games’ parent company as a “very reasonable” person, which is why they were able to secure the extra time needed to finish development.

The topic came up during a recent interview between Strauss Zelnick and the Wall Street Journal . The Take-Two Interactive executive recalled that being told the release date needed to be pushed back was not ideal, but ultimately says he approved the decision to ensure the quality of the product.

“Your mission is to create the best entertainment on Earth, and part of your three-pillar strategy is to be the most creative. And sometimes you have to make those costly and uncomfortable decisions in service of that mission and those goals.”

GTA VI suffered two delays, changing its official release date twice.

While discussing the matter, Strauss Zelnick pointed out that many companies have an excellent vision, a well-defined strategy, and an established culture, but sometimes end up doing things that contradict all of those principles. He explained that moments like these put everyone involved to the test.

The Take-Two Interactive CEO acknowledged that some developers choose to stick to an established release schedule at all costs, leading them to launch games even when they are not ready. Although he did not mention any names, he clearly took a shot at Cyberpunk 2077 .

“I’m not going to blame any competitor, but if you know anything about the videogame industry, you’ll remember that in recent years there was a high-profile launch that fell into this category: they released it, and then had to pull it from the market after launch because it didn’t work,” Strauss Zelnick commented.

Of course, several other games have also had to be removed from digital storefronts after launching with serious problems. One of the most recent examples is SEGA’s Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition . However, to be fair, CD Projekt RED’s RPG is one of the few cases that fit the category of “high-profile launches.”

Cyberpunk 2077 debuted in 2020, but all of its versions suffered from technical issues, bugs, and other errors that hurt the experience. As a result, the game was removed from Sony’s PlayStation Store, and the developers offered refunds. The controversy also led to a class-action lawsuit against CD Projekt RED.

items.title: This Cyberpunk 2077 graphics overhaul has managed to get me hyped for Project Orion
items.summary: It's going to be many, many years before the sequel arrives though 😅
items.content:
Project Orion is years away, but mods like this remind me of just how excited I am.

Project Orion , a sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , is in development, but it’s a game that I try not to think about too often.

That’s largely due to the fact that its arrival is a long way off, and I’m trying to save myself some of the impatience I’ve experienced with the likes of Grand Theft Auto VI and The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel.

CD Projekt RED is hard at work developing The Witcher IV , which is due out in 2028. Project Orion is not set to become the studio’s main focus until following The Witcher IV ’s launch.

Given the fact that developers won’t want to rush Project Orion and repeat Cyberpunk 2077 ’s mistakes, it places the game as potentially arriving in the mid 2030s.

You’re perhaps seeing my logic now for almost pretending the project doesn’t exist, but it was recently brought to the forefront of my attention thanks to an awesome new mod.

‘ Atmos 2077 ’ is an incredible new graphical overhaul mod for Cyberpunk 2077 with results so impressive that I immediately started pondering what Project Orion might look like.

Created by NexusMods user robindubronx, ‘Atmos 2077’ is a very comprehensive offering, introducing new volumetric clouds to Cyberpunk 2077 , as well as new rain and thunderstorm effects, including dynamic raindrops on your car’s windshield.

You should also expect rainbows, ballistic missile trails in the sky, and more. As you’ve likely gathered, it’s a weather-based mod, but one that hugely boosts the immersive experience of navigating Night City.

That’s no easy feat to pull off because Night City is arguably one of gaming’s most immersive open worlds anyway, but ‘Atmos 2077’ just manages to refine what it offers perfectly.

“Night City runs on neon, chrome, and rain. In the vanilla game, the rain is a flat curtain of streaks under a painted sky,” begins the mod’s creator.

“Atmos 2077 rewires the whole atmosphere: volumetric clouds you can read like a weather map, real rain that lands, glass that holds water, storms that light up from inside, and rainbows when the sun cuts back through.”

Everything within the mod is drawn inside the game’s own renderer via REDgraph, so no ReShade or overlay was used.

The mod’s storms are incredibly cozy, if that’s not a weird thing to say. There’s something quite mesmerising about driving Night City’s streets amid a biblical storm.

items.title: 10 Best Open World Games with Character Creation, Ranked
items.summary: Open-world games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077 are better because of their character creators.
items.content:
Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Mandi Odoerfer Published Nov 12, 2026, 10:15 PM EST Mandi has been writing about comics and video games for more than ten years and has been reading and playing them her entire life. Her writing has been featured at TapTap , GameZone , US Gamer, and many other sites. She joined CBR in 2024, where she works as a writer and editor, covering video games and comic books. In her downtime, she occasionally muses about anime, RPGs, and the best Steam demos on her Substack, Cartoon Ghost , though she often finds herself retreating to the comfort of her favorite games. Mandi is currently replaying the entire Pokémon series, starting with Red & Blue . Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Open-world games don't always let players create their own characters, but many of the best games in the genre have in-depth character creation tools. Games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077 let players make a character of their choosing, with in-depth tools that can bring all kinds of concepts to life.

Not only do many open-world games with character creators give players extreme control over their character's appearance, but many allow them to customize their characters in other ways as well, such as determining their background and assigning them with specific skills. When done well, character creation can feel like its own game.

Not many games offer the level of player agency that Mount and Blade II: Bannerlord does. It's a mixture of genres, blending tactical gameplay with first and third-person real-time combat, along with RPG elements and settlement creation. Even the main narrative can be ignored with minimal consequences.

On top of that, players can customize their character's appearance, choose their civilization of origin, and answer a series of questions to build a background that influences their skills. After that, players are free to pursue their own path, whether as a merchant, a trusted general commanding a large army, or a leader of a smaller mercenary band working for the highest bidder.

Rip Mystery Packs of Graded Cards & Collectibles

Japanese Pokémon Center 20th Anniversary Promo · PSA 10

Must be 18+/19+ to participate depending on jurisdiction.

code vein 2 ichor jail Image via Bandai Namco While it can be fun to create a character from scratch, many of the best video game character creators also let players recreate their favorite characters from other properties. Few games are as good at this as Code Vein and its open-world sequel, Code Vein II , which give players the tools to make almost any anime character.

Many of the most popular anime characters of all time have been recreated in Code Vein II , including Gojo Satoru from Jujutsu Kaisen and Mikasa Ackerman from Attack on Titan . It's a game that no anime fan who loves character creators should miss.

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Image via FromSoftware Elden Ring has become a legendary title in the years since its release, and only a few games in the genre can surpass it . While FromSoftware's games have always been known for the amount of freedom they allow players, Elden Ring is the most open by far, with an open world that's fascinating to explore.

There's excellent character customization in Elden Ring , but while players can choose their protagonist's gender, age, class, keepsakes, and physical appearance, the most exciting aspect is the freedom players have over character builds. There are 10 starting classes in Elden Ring , and choosing the right build can make the game far more approachable.

Image via Bethesda While Fallout 4 has been criticized for its story, it offers the most expansive and free open world in the franchise. The Green Jewel of the Commonwealth, Diamond City, doesn't quite measure up to iconic locations like New Vegas, Rivet City, or Megaton, but in this game, it doesn't matter. Players can create a settlement from scratch and make it their own.

Character customization is crucial in video games, and games like Baldur's Gate III, Fallout 4, and Starfield have many more options than others.

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter If you're a fan of CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, you might have been excited about some of the headlines appearing in the past couple of days. 'New Cyberpunk 2077 game reveals official gameplay,' one read. ‘Cyberpunk 2077 returns with ambitious new release,' was another. One even suggested that a new Cyberpunk 2077 was going to steal GTA 6's thunder.

Alas, some fans might have been disappointed to read those stories and discover that the new game is more analogue than what they might have imagined. Given how long it takes to make an AAA video game, it was highly unlikely that we would get Cyberpunk 2077 2 in 2027 – 2028 maybe, but even that's a very optimistic estimate.

The new Cyberpunk 2077 is, in fact, a board game. But don't write it off, it follows in a long traditional of video game to board game transitions, and some of them have been quite good.

Watch On Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game looks set to do justice to the video game's vast lore and worldbuilding in its physical scale. The eight-minute unboxing video above reveals just how huge it is with the various miniatures, mission cards, character boards and gameplay expansions

Published by Go On Board, it's billed as a cooperative, story-driven campaign game. Players take on the roles of Edgerunners, exploring Night City and completing 13 multi-stage missions. A timer mechanic is intended to replicate the paced of the action of the video game.

Dispatch's new Deluxe Edition lets you play the whole game as storyboard animatics This tabletop console brings family game night back, and it just got $60 cheaper GTA 6's leak exposes the uncomfortable truth about digital-only games The game follows the release of the trading card game Cyberpunk TCG. If its successful, it should be able to evolve alongside the video game franchise for many years.

The trend of turning video games into board games has exploded over the past decade, with crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter or Gamefound playing a big role in helping the physical adaptations get off the ground. They also tap into the growing interest in physical media and analogue tech as a respite from digital screen time, providing a physical social experience.

Critical reception has been a bit of a mixed bag. Some have been heralded as masterpieces, others are criticised as overpriced miniature-fests that prioritise plastic over playable design.

The most successful adaptations are those that don't just copy-paste the digital game, but translate its feeling and core loops into smart, physical mechanics. Slay the Spire: The Board Game is much loved for how it turned a single-player digital roguelike and turning it into cooperative tabletop deck-builder, and Frostpunk succeeded in bringing the punishing decision-making of digital survival games to the table.

On a very different note, the cosy Dorfromantik: The Board Game captured the zen-like puzzle game vibe of its digital counterpart.

Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival is the horror game AAA publishers have been too prudish to make The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past's lush new location and remaster improvements have me excited to be Geralt again GTA 6 will “raise the bar” by ignoring game industry trends, says Helldivers 2 dev On the other hand, Dark Souls: The Board Game was seen by some as being tedious and repetitive despite its gorgeous miniatures.

Board games can also be the ultimate collector's item for video game fans. Even if a $200 Elden Ring or Resident Evil board games only hits the table once or twice a year, the gorgeous, highly detailed miniatures also serve as display pieces.

items.title: New Cyberpunk 2077 Game Officially Reveals Brand-New Gameplay
‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Officially Returns Next Year With Ambitious New Release
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is officially set to return in 2027 with the franchise's first tabletop game, allowing players to experience new layers of Night City.
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 Image via CD Projekt Red Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Adam Blevins Published Jul 15, 2026, 2:00 PM EDT Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios , House of the Dragon , and Planet of the Apes . He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday , The Penguin , Star Wars: Skeleton Crew , and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant . You can find him on X , LinkedIn , and Muckrack . Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 11 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Gaming has reached nearly unprecedented levels of hype in 2026, which is mostly due to the biggest launch the industry has seen in years, Grand Theft Auto 6 . After several delays, Rockstar has finally confirmed that GTA 6 will launch on November 19, and pre-orders for the game are officially live as of a few weeks ago, confirming that it will now launch on schedule. The next big gaming launch of the year before GTA 6 comes when Insomniac Games releases its next big Marvel project, Wolverine , starring Liam McIntyre as the new Logan. This will be Insomniac’s first game since Spider-Man 2 in 2023. The biggest release of 2026 so far came not long ago with the premiere of 007 First Light , the Patrick Gibson -starring James Bond game developed by IO Interactive , the same studio behind the Hitman games.

There have been plenty of big gaming properties to emerge in the last 10 years, but few have become as popular as Cyberpunk 2077 , which launched in 2020 as one of the most problematic releases in modern gaming history. The game has since found redemption with quality of life updates, DLCs like Phantom Liberty , and even a Netflix TV show returning for Season 2 this year. CD Projekt Red has confirmed it’s working on another Cyberpunk game, but with The Witcher 4 being understandably prioritized over the new Cyberpunk game, it’s unlikely it will be released anytime in the next few years. Still, Cyberpunk fans do have a new release coming much sooner to be excited about, as it was recently announced over on GameFound that Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game is expected to launch before the end of 2027.

Close Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1263901037"] = '" Close Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound "'; Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game is a new sci-fi expansion launching in 2027, and it will be the first time in franchise history that the property has been adapted into tabletop format . The crowdfunded project has already raised an impressive $11.8 million from over 32,000 backers, giving the game a more expensive budget to work with than many other projects in the same genre. Tabletop may not be every gamer’s style, but this new release is perfect for fans who just can’t wait for the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel before experiencing new content from Night City. The official description for the game reads as follows:

“Welcome to Night City, the metropolis of the future. Here, the local blends with the global, and the past, present, and future merge into one. ‘It's a blitz through the underbelly of this city, where you fight, hack, and hustle your way to the top. Just like the good old days.'

Each Player controls one Character – an Edgerunner. With the guidance of the App and the Locations Map, Players will decide which Mission to take. Through a series of real-time Fights and Cooldowns between them, Players must complete the Main Objectives provided by the Mission card’s description. Each Character has a deck with Action cards and unique features specific to them.

The main part of the game will happen in Sequential Timed Action Phase Fight segments, managed by the App. After the signal, Players look at their hands, choose an Active Player, and play their turns one after the other, starting with the Active Player, until the time runs out.”

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of all things Cyberpunk .

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
